operator_tests.coverage: Independent FP8/BF16 oracle, 4096 FP4 code/scale cases, 409 multirow checks, 1008 mode/split comparisons and repeated GPU 0/1/0 transitions

notes: The original V4.1 NVFP4 cache borrows registered NUMA block-32 weights without a host weight snapshot. Expert math preserves block-32 FP8 activation quantization, route weighting before down-input quantization, clipping, BF16 projection boundaries and ordered per-expert reduction.

One model load uses equal serial layer placement on two GPUs. The full benchmark uses a fixed 8 GiB budget per GPU, matching the preceding Q2 dual-GPU test. Startup warmup allocates these caches before Python controls; the controls disable dispatch while retaining the payload. Controls set_moe_cuda_cache(0) to disable dispatch; retained cache records stay allocated during formal controls.

Off-cache warmups generate 64 short ordinary tokens, 64 short DSpark tokens and the long retrieval response. Then cache warmups generate 256 short ordinary tokens, 256 short DSpark tokens and the long retrieval response. Three alternating formal short requests per mode, arithmetic/code fixtures, three alternating long DSpark requests per mode and one long ordinary control per mode follow.

Cache counters synchronize CUDA outside request timing. The V4.1 route trace is enabled at its built-in reporting intervals. Lookup counters do not represent all NUMA routes; route traces report actual CPU/GPU splits.

CUDA cache retains live residency and adaptive scheduling across requests. Numerical differences can change generated text, draft acceptance and route selection; compare paired outputs and acceptance before attributing throughput changes solely to compute acceleration.
Timing is native launch to first token and then first-to-last token throughput; excludes loading, tokenization and HTTP. Prefix/history caching is disabled. Fast prefill is enabled.
The long retrieval task only generates about 30 tokens. Functional fixtures and these timing results do not establish complete model accuracy or general conversation performance.

The preceding Q2 dual-GPU reference uses the same installed library, 28 CPU threads, serial device map, prompts, output limits, sampling parameters, 8 GiB per GPU, KV dtype, fast-prefill setting and warmup/repeat schedule. The two model formats use different processes; output and draft-acceptance changes must be considered before attributing throughput differences solely to kernels. Loading times use uncontrolled file page caches.
